title: Navigating Communication Barriers in Dementia Care
learning_goal: Apply therapeutic communication techniques and identify nontherapeutic communication to effectively interact with a patient experiencing cognitive and emotional communication barriers.
target_audience: Nursing students and early-career registered nurses.
visual_style: 2D semi-flat limited-animation style with dynamic but constrained movement. Characters express emotion through head turns, nods, hand gestures, subtle posture shifts, and facial expressions. Mouth movement suggests speech without exact phoneme matching.

appearance.hair: Black, styled in short neat locs
appearance.uniform: Royal blue medical scrubs with a stethoscope around her neck
appearance.distinguishing_features: Warm, expressive eyes and a calm demeanor

appearance.uniform: Light blue hospital gown over comfortable sweatpants
appearance.distinguishing_features: Wears wire-rimmed glasses, often has furrowed brows indicating confusion or worry

setting.scene_description: A standard, clean hospital room with a patient bed, a small bedside table, and a window. A small duffel bag is on the bed.

lighting.source: Overhead fluorescent lights mixed with soft natural light from the window

background_furniture.name: Hospital Bed
background_furniture.description: Adjustable bed with white linens, slightly elevated.

background_furniture.name: Bedside Table
background_furniture.description: A small rolling table with a water pitcher and a cup.

background_furniture.name: Guest Chair
background_furniture.description: A comfortable vinyl armchair near the window.

camera.perspective: Medium shot capturing both characters to show nonverbal interactions clearly.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara enters the room to find Arthur packing his belongings, displaying visible anxiety and acting on a dementia-related delusion.
scenes.character_actions: Arthur is hurriedly stuffing a pair of socks into a small duffel bag on his bed. Clara walks in slowly, keeping her hands visible and her posture open.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing by the side of the bed, facing the bag.
Standing near the doorway, observing Arthur.

dialogue.line: I have to catch the bus. Buster hasn't eaten since this morning, and he gets scared when it's dark.
dialogue.character_position: Standing by the side of the bed, facing the bag.

audio.sound_effects: Rustling of fabric as Arthur packs.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara uses false reassurance, causing Arthur to feel misunderstood and more anxious.
scenes.character_actions: Clara smiles broadly and waves a hand dismissively. Arthur turns to her, gripping his bag tightly, his face showing increased distress.

dialogue.line: Don't worry, Mr. Vance, everything is perfectly fine. You can just relax in bed.
Nothing is fine! You don't understand me at all. I need to leave right now!

scenes.scene_summary: Clara successfully uses therapeutic communication by sharing observations, prompting Arthur to open up.
scenes.character_actions: Clara takes a step closer, maintaining gentle eye contact and a relaxed posture. Arthur stops packing and looks at her, his shoulders dropping slightly.

dialogue.line: You seem very focused on packing, Mr. Vance. Are you worried about something?
dialogue.character_position: Moving slowly toward the center of the room.

dialogue.line: I am worried. Buster is all alone at home, and he needs his dinner.
dialogue.character_position: Standing by the bed, looking at Clara.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara interrogates Arthur, causing him to become defensive.
scenes.character_actions: Clara crosses her arms slightly. Arthur glares at her, his posture becoming rigid.

dialogue.line: Why are you packing your bags, Mr. Vance? You know you aren't discharged yet.
Don't interrogate me! I'm leaving because I have responsibilities, unlike the people in this place!

scenes.scene_summary: Arthur continues to focus on his dog, Buster. Clara knows from the chart that Buster passed away years ago.
scenes.character_actions: Arthur holds a pair of socks, looking down at them sadly. Clara is standing near him, listening attentively.

initial_character_positions.position: Standing a few feet away from Arthur.

dialogue.line: He's such a good dog, but he whines when he's hungry. I really have to get home to him.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara changes the subject, making Arthur feel ignored and distressed.
scenes.character_actions: Clara points toward the bedside table. Arthur looks away from her, shaking his head in frustration.

dialogue.line: Let's not worry about the dog right now. It's time to take your evening medication.
I don't want any medication! Are you even listening to me? My dog needs me!
dialogue.character_position: Standing by the bed, turning away.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara argues with Arthur by presenting harsh facts, causing severe agitation.
scenes.character_actions: Clara shakes her head, speaking firmly. Arthur's eyes widen with anger and he points a finger at her.

dialogue.line: Mr. Vance, your family told us Buster passed away five years ago. You are in the hospital.
You're lying! You're trying to keep me away from him! Get out of my room!
dialogue.character_position: Standing by the bed, raising his voice.

scenes.scene_summary: Clara uses empathy and active listening to validate Arthur's feelings, successfully calming him down.
scenes.character_actions: Clara nods compassionately. Arthur's facial expression softens, and he places the socks down on the bed, looking warmly at Clara.

dialogue.line: It sounds like you take wonderful care of Buster. Tell me more about him.
He's a golden retriever... he always waits for me right by the front door.
He sounds like a wonderful companion. Let's sit down in this chair, and you can tell me about his favorite treats.
dialogue.character_position: Gesturing gently toward the guest chair.

audio.sound_effects: Soft rustling as Arthur puts the bag down.

decision_points.question_text: How should Nurse Clara initiate communication with Mr. Vance to address his anxiety?

choices.text: Approach slowly and share observations: "You seem very focused on packing, Mr. Vance. Are you worried about something?"
Provide comfort through an automatic response: "Don't worry, Mr. Vance, everything is perfectly fine. You can just relax in bed."
choices.misconception: Giving false reassurance and automatic responses are nontherapeutic communication techniques that dismiss the patient's valid feelings and shut down communication.

choices.text: Ask for his reasoning: "Why are you packing your bags, Mr. Vance? You know you aren't discharged yet."
choices.misconception: Asking "why" questions acts as an interrogation, which is a nontherapeutic communication technique that often causes patients to become defensive.

decision_points.question_text: How should Nurse Clara respond to Mr. Vance's distress about his deceased dog?

choices.text: Share empathy and actively listen: "It sounds like you take wonderful care of Buster. Tell me more about him."
Redirect him to the present: "Let's not worry about the dog right now. It's time to take your evening medication."
choices.misconception: Changing the subject is a nontherapeutic technique that makes the patient feel disrespected and ignored, damaging the nurse-patient relationship.

choices.text: Provide factual reality orientation: "Mr. Vance, your family told us Buster passed away five years ago. You are in the hospital."
choices.misconception: Arguing with or directly challenging a patient's reality, especially when they have cognitive impairments, is a nontherapeutic technique that causes anger and destroys trust.
